 Judgment

The petitioner has filed this Petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- for the Death of one Smt. Pilliyamma @ Pilli @ Valli @ Velli in a road traffic accident dated 28.09.2019.
2.

The case of the Petitioner in brief is that:
On 28.09.2019, when the deceased Smt. Pilliyamma @ Pilli @ Valli @ Velli was crossing the Road Opp. to SLN Complex, Annapoorna Junction, Bengaluru city,
within the jurisdiction of VV Puram Traffic Police Station, Bengaluru City, a private Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-06-C-5778 came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner, endangering SCCH-25 human life and dashed against the deceased.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Due to impact she fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

3. It is the further case of the petitioner that, immediately after the accident the deceased was rushed to the Victoria Hospital for treatment but, she succumbed to the injuries on the same day at 3.00pm.
The Post Mortem was conducted at Victoria Hospital, Bangalore.
At the time of accident deceased was hale and healthy, doing Coolie work and earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
The petitioner lost loving and care taking mother.

Due to the sudden demise of the deceased Smt.
Pilliyamma @ Pilli @ Valli @ Velli, she is put to mental shock and agony.
The accident took place solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Private Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-06-C-5778.

The VV Puram Traffic Police have registered a case against the driver of the Private Bus in Cr.NO.80/2019 for the offences p/u/sec.279, 337 & 304A of IPC.
SCCH-25 The respondents being the owner and insurer of the Private Bus are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence this petition.
4. In response to the service of notice, the Respondents appeared through their respective counsels and filed separate written statements.

5. The objections of the 1st respondent:
He has denied all the petition averments except admitting the ownership of the Private Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-06-C-5778 and the bus was insured with the 2 nd respondent and the policy was in existence as on the date of accident.
The accident occurred solely due to the negligence of the deceased herself for not following and observing the traffic rules.
The driver of the alleged bus was having a valid DL as on the date of accident.
There is no negligence on the part of the driver of the said bus.
Further stated that the petitioner is not dependent of the deceased.
He has denied the age, income, avocation of the deceased and the SCCH-25 compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition.

6. The objections of the 2nd respondent:

sentences.text: It has stated that, the petition is not maintainable either on law or on facts.
It has admitted the issuance of policy in respect of the offending vehicle/respondent No.1 for the private bus bearing No.KA-06-C-5778.
The driver of the vehicle was not having valid DL to drive the Bus.
There was a non compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of M.V. Act.
The accident was caused due to the negligence of the deceased.
It has denied the involvement of the vehicle in the accident and the vehicle is falsely implicated.
It has denied the age, occupation, income and averred that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive.
Hence prayed for dismissal of the petition.

7. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:
SCCH-25 1. Whether the Petitioner proves that, she is the legal heir of the deceased Smt.
Pilliyamma @ Pilli @ Valli @ Velli?
2.

Whether the Petitioner proves that, Smt. Pilliyamma @ Pilli @ Valli @ Velli was died on account of Road Traffic Accident took place on Opp. Complex, Annapoorna Junction, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Bus bearing Reg.No.KA- 06-C-5778 dated 28.09.2019 at about 12.55pm?

3. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from whom payable 4. What Order or Award?
8.
In order to prove her case, the Petitioner has examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 10 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.10.
On the other side, the Respondent No.2 got examined Mr. Kiran Kumar - SDA, Bengaluru RTO and got marked Exs.R.1 to R.3.

It has also examined its Official/Administrative Manager Mr. Prashanth N.G. as RW.2 and got marked Exs.R.4 & 5.
9.
Heard both the Counsels and perused the materials on record.
SCCH-25 10.
My finding to the above issues are as follows:-

Issue Nos.1 & 2: In the affirmative Issue No.3 : In the affirmative, Issue No.4 : As per final order for the Following:
REASONS 11.

Issue No.1:

The Petitioner to prove her relationship has examined herself as PW.1.
PW.1 has specifically spoken about their relationship in her chief-examination.
Apart from that, to prove the relationship, she has produced her notarized copy of Aadhar Card and the deceased's Voter's ID Card at Exs.P.9 & 10.
She has produced Inquest Mahazar at Ex.P.7.

In the Aadhar Card of the petitioner her husband's name is mentioned and in the Voter's ID Card of the deceased, her husband's name is mentioned as Krishna which can be seen in the Inquest Mahazar also.
In the Inquest Mahazar it can be seen that the deceased daughter's name is mentioned as Velangani who is the petitioner.
These documents have not been seriously disputed by the Respondent No.2.
The SCCH-25 Respondent No.2 has not produced any contrary documents to dispute and rebut the contents of documents produced by the Petitioner.
As such, there are no reasons to discard the oral and documentary evidence produced by the Petitioner.
Under such circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 and the documents, this court is of the opinion that the petitioner is the daughter of the deceased.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:

The Petitioner to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Private Bus bearing No.KA-06-C-5778 has examined herself as PW.1 and produced documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.8.
PW.1 has reiterated the averments of the petition in her affidavit filed in lieu of her chief examination.
On the other side, the Respondent Nos.1 & 2 have denied the involvement and negligence of the offending vehicle.
SCCH-25 13

. The documents produced by the petitioner such as the FIR in Cr.No.80/2019 of V V Puram Police with FIS, spot sketch, spot mahazar, IMV report, PM report, Inquest mahazar and the charge sheet as per Exs.P.1 to P.8 are all public documents and have initial presumptive value under law.
These documents fully and completely corroborate with the evidence of PW.1.

The investigation officer in crime No.80/2019 of VV Puram Police has conducted the investigation in detail and has filed the charge sheet against the driver of the Private Bus bearing No.KA-06-C-5778, holding that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.
During the cross examination of PW.1 by the respondent No.2, she has admitted that the accident would not have occurred that the deceased had used the underpass.
She has further admitted that in the accident spot pedestrian cannot cross the road.
14. The Inquest mahazar produced as per Ex.P.7 and PM report produced as per Ex.P.6 clearly show that 'Death is SCCH-25 due to shock and Hemorrhage as a result of multiple Injuries sustained".

Even though the petitioner has admitted that the accident occurred since her mother did not use the underpass, the Bus driver could have avoided the accident if he was not driving the bus in a rash and negligent manner.
The deceased was more than 65 years old and rustic villager.

Therefore, on Velangini vs Vijayakumar on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165989297/
4 perusal of police documents, it is clear that the accident occurred due to the negligence in driving by the Driver of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 in the Affirmative.
15. Issue No. 3:
PW.1 has specifically spoken before this court that due to the untimely death of the deceased, she has lost her loving and care taking mother.
She has further deposed that she has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards conveyance, transportation of dead body and for performing the funeral ceremonies.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation as per the following discussion.
SCCH-25 Monthly income 16.
According to the petitioner the deceased was doing Coolie work and earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
To prove the income of the deceased the petitioner has not produced any documents such as Bank statement etc., nor has she examined any witness.
The accident occurred in the year 2019.
Under such circumstances, this court deems it to fix the income of the deceased notionally at Rs.14,000/- per month for calculating the compensation.
Age of the deceased 17.
In so far as age of the deceased is concerned, the petitioner has produced notarized copy of Voter's ID of the deceased as per Ex.P.10.
As per Ex.P.10 the deceased was aged about 47 years.
This is a public document and has got presumptive value under law.
This shows that as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased was 47 years.
SCCH-25 (i) LOSS OF DEPENDENCY AND FUTURE PROSPECTS:-
As per the principles of law laid down in the case of Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation, appropriate multiplier applicable to her age is 13.

the deceased had a daughter who is aged about 46 years, married, and residing with her husband.
As such, it can be seen that she was not depending on the deceased.
Therefore, she is not be considered as dependent of the deceased and not entitled to any amount under this head.

ii) LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:-
In Magma General Insurance company Limited Vs. Nanuram (2018) 18 SCC 130

iii) TRANSPORTATION AND FUNERAL EXPENSES:-
PW.1 has stated that she has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards, transportation of dead body, funeral expenses and obsequies etc..
In this regard the petitioner has not produced any bills pertaining to the above said expenses.
However, there are expenses during the death of a person for which documents cannot be maintained.
Therefore, in the interest of SCCH-25 justice, the petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.

iv) LOSS OF ESTATE:-
As mentioned above
, the deceased was earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month.
Out of this, she was spending 1/2 of her income towards personal expenses.
Such being the case, out of this, certainly the deceased would have saved some amount and created estate in favor of the Petitioner.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.20,000/- under the head of loss of estate.
As such, in total, the Petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.80,000/-.
LIABILITY 20.
The respondent No.2 has contended that the Private bus did not have valid permit as on the date of accident.
In this regard the respondent No.2 has examined Mr.Kiran Kumar, SDA at RTO as RW.1 and got marked Exs.R.1 to R.3 authorization letter, permit (3 pages) and Notice issued to permit holder (2 in nos.).
In his examination SCCH-25 in chief he has stated that the vehicle had carriage permit from 23.11.1999 to 19.11.2014 to be renewed every 5 years.
But after 2014 the permit was not renewed and was canceled by the Tribunal.
The RTO Office had issued notice to the owner of the vehicle to stop plying.
He has further stated that as on the date of accident the bus did not have a valid permit.
During the cross examination of RW.1, he has admitted that the vehicle bearing No.KA-06-C-5778 was registered in Tumkur RTO.
The Respondent No.2 also got examined its official/Administrative Manager as RW.2 and got marked Exs.R.4 and R.5 authorization letter and copy of policy.
During the cross examination of the RW.2, he has stated that the insured vehicle was first registered in Tumkur RTO and was later transferred to KR Puram RTO.
There is no mention about the Permit in the charge sheet that the insured vehicle did not have permit.
Therefore, it is clear that as on the date of accident, the offending vehicle did not have a Permit to ply the Bus on road.
But in contravention of the orders of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, the Bus was being plied on SCCH-25 the Road.

For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:-
SCCH-25 ORDER
The Petition filed by the Petitioner under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for Compensation of Rs.80,000/- (Rupees Eighty Thousand only) along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.

The respondent No.2 is directed to pay the compensation to the petitioner and shall de- posit the Award amount and interest before this Tribunal within 60 days from the date of this Judgment and later recover the same from the respondent No.1.
On deposit of the award amount and inter- est, it shall be released to the petitioner by way of e-payment with proper identification and due acknowledgment.
The Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
SCCH-25 Draw Award accordingly.
